title: Undecidable quantum storage with seven elementary gates
description: Can the noise rate of one fixed local circuit encode an undecidable quantum-storage problem? Yes: we construct a three-dimensional medium, using only X, H, CNOT, Toffoli, reset, dephasing and identity, whose storage behaviour on explicit rate windows is as hard to decide as the halting problem. A separate construction handles each of whole-site and independent single-qubit depolarization after every layer. Computable disjoint rational rate windows select universal-machine inputs. For each nonhalting input, one computable encoder stores a reference-entangled qubit for a fixed positive multiple of the side length, at every size above a computable input-dependent threshold. On halting windows, every encoding fails after a time uniform in size and rate. A linear whole-channel upper bound makes the nonhalting storage scale sharp; certification of the explicit circuits is Π⁰₁-complete, with exact rational finite tests. The proof combines a noisy classical hierarchical calendar with concatenated binary quantum codes and a two-copy channel extension. A separate four-dimensional medium, under single-qubit depolarization only, has both an uncomputable storage diagram and a designed, decidable window of exponential storage. Interactions are finite-range rather than nearest-neighbour, constants are astronomical, and every finite sample eventually forgets.
notes: Preprint. It has not been peer reviewed. The authors have not independently verified the mathematical arguments; the paper's section 'How this work was done' describes the model-based construction and the cross-family checks.
